LOCAL ACTION / SHARED HORIZONS
Notice a need · Build an idea · Take action · Share what you learn
01 / The movement

A starting point
should never be
a stopping point.

Talent and ideas exist everywhere. Access to support does not. ZLYM exists to help close that distance.

“You do not have to wait for the perfect opportunity, the perfect place, or someone else to begin.”

Zero Line Youth Movement is a global youth-led initiative built around a simple belief: young people should not need to leave their communities to create meaningful change in them.

A young person may see a problem in their school, town, or neighborhood and have the motivation to do something about it — but lack a team, a mentor, practical tools, or even a clear first step. ZLYM is designed to help make that first step possible.

The movement is still at its beginning. It is being built step by step, with the people who choose to take part — not around the idea of collecting names or certificates, but around doing work that matters.

02 / How it works

From a local question
to a shared action.

Members are not just audience members. They are the people who notice, shape, lead, and learn from projects in their own communities.

01

Notice

Identify a real need, gap, or overlooked possibility in your local community.

02

Shape

Turn what you noticed into a clear, realistic project with a purpose and a plan.

03

Build

Work with your team, access guidance, and take practical steps toward implementation.

04

Pass it on

Share what worked, what did not, and what others can learn or adapt elsewhere.

Local ownershipProjects respond to real needs identified by the people who live them.
Shared learningMembers exchange knowledge, methods, and honest lessons across borders.
Real contributionParticipation is measured by meaningful effort, not titles or attendance.

04 / Across borders

Different places.
Connected efforts.

A project may begin in one school or one small town, but the learning does not have to stay there. Through international collaboration, members can exchange approaches, compare local realities, and adapt ideas thoughtfully — without assuming that one solution fits every community.

The goal is not to make every place look the same. It is to let people learn from one another while creating change that makes sense where they are.

Local roots · Global connections
05 / Our people

A network built
by its members.

No names, country list, or team profiles are published here until participation is confirmed. This space will grow with the actual community — not with placeholder profiles.
06 / Founder
ZL.

It began with
one local gap.

ZLYM grew out of a personal experience: trying to pursue research opportunities from Minya, in Upper Egypt, and realizing how much harder it can be to find guidance, resources, and a supportive environment outside major opportunity centers. Instead of treating that gap as a reason to wait, I began helping students around me find pathways, learn independently, and work on ideas of their own.

That local experience became a bigger question: what if young people in different places could help one another build what their communities are missing? ZLYM is my attempt to turn that question into a structure others can shape, lead, and carry forward.

Rawan Adel Abdulmalik

08 / Questions

Good questions
come first.

A few things worth knowing before you join.

Is ZLYM a scholarship or opportunity announcement page?

No. Its central purpose is to help young people identify local needs, develop projects, and learn through action and collaboration. Information may be shared when useful, but announcements are not the movement's main work.

Do I need to have a project idea before joining?

No. Curiosity, commitment, and willingness to contribute are a good starting point. Members can learn how to understand a need and shape an idea with support.

Does ZLYM operate in every country already?

Not yet. ZLYM is in its founding stage. Country representation will be announced only after ambassadors are confirmed.

Is participation only online?

The network connects members online, while local projects may take place in communities. Any in-person activity must be planned responsibly and follow appropriate safeguarding and guardian-consent requirements.

How can an organization collaborate with ZLYM?

Use the partnership contact route to introduce your organization, the community you serve, and the kind of collaboration you have in mind.
